title: A layer is a map
caption: One dense layer: previous activations times a weight matrix plus a bias, then an element-wise nonlinearity. A network is this map composed L times; without f the composition collapses to a single linear map and depth buys nothing.

symbols.name: layer output
symbols.meaning: activations leaving layer l (B x n_l matrix at batch B)

symbols.name: layer input
symbols.meaning: activations arriving from the previous layer (or the raw example for l = 1)

symbols.name: weight matrix
symbols.meaning: n_{l-1} x n_l parameters; one MAC per weight per example

symbols.name: bias vector
symbols.meaning: n_l added parameters, broadcast across the batch

symbols.name: activation
symbols.meaning: element-wise nonlinearity (ReLU, sigmoid, softmax); the load-bearing term

title: Cost from shapes
caption: Parameters, per-example work, and retained-activation memory all read off the layer widths before any code runs. Width enters quadratically (every weight sits in a product), depth linearly but adds sequential steps and saved activations. For 784-128-64-10: P = 109,386, Ops = 218,368 FLOPs/digit.

symbols.name: parameter count
symbols.meaning: weights plus biases; the persistent memory term

symbols.name: fan-in plus bias
symbols.meaning: inputs per neuron including the bias column

symbols.name: per-example FLOPs
symbols.meaning: 2 per MAC (multiply + add); 218,368 for the running network

symbols.name: activation memory
symbols.meaning: bytes held for outputs at batch B; the inference-buffer term

symbols.name: layer MACs
symbols.meaning: multiply-accumulates per example; x2 for FLOPs

symbols.name: batch size
symbols.meaning: multiplies retained activations only, not parameters

symbols.name: depth
symbols.meaning: layer count; also the number of chain-rule factors and saved activation sets

title: Cross-entropy with fused softmax gradient
caption: Against a one-hot label the full cross-entropy sum collapses to the negative log of the correct-class probability. Fused with softmax, each logit's gradient is predicted mass minus target: wrong classes push down by p, the right class up by 1 - p. The 'seven read as three' example: loss -log(0.1) = 2.30, gradients +0.6 on 'three', -0.9 on 'seven'.

symbols.name: correct-class probability
symbols.meaning: softmax output on the true label; log grows sharply near zero, punishing confident errors

symbols.name: logit j
symbols.meaning: raw pre-softmax score for class j

symbols.name: predicted mass
symbols.meaning: softmax probability assigned to class j

symbols.name: target
symbols.meaning: one-hot label: 1 on the true class, 0 elsewhere

title: Two backward products per layer
latex: \frac{\partial L}{\partial W^{(l)}} = {A^{(l-1)}}^{\!\!T}\frac{\partial L}{\partial Z^{(l)}}, \qquad \frac{\partial L}{\partial A^{(l-1)}} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial Z^{(l)}}{W^{(l)}}^{\!\!T}
caption: A dense layer's backward pass runs two matrix products of forward size: one for the weight gradient and one to carry the signal to the previous layer. That is the origin of the 3x rule, one forward product plus two backward products per layer. The first layer skips its input gradient, so the running network lands near 2.08x.

symbols.name: weight gradient
symbols.meaning: what the optimizer consumes; one forward-size matmul (A^T dZ)

symbols.name: input gradient
symbols.meaning: signal carried to the previous layer; second forward-size matmul (dZ W^T)

symbols.name: pre-activation error
symbols.meaning: output error masked by f'(Z); the Hadamard-product term

symbols.name: saved input
symbols.meaning: forward activations that must stay live until this point in the backward pass

symbols.name: weights
symbols.meaning: the forward matrix transposed for the input-gradient product

title: Four kinds of state
latex: M_{train} \approx W + G + O + A_{saved}, \qquad M_{infer} \approx W + \max_l\big(A^{(l)} + A^{(l+1)}\big)
caption: Training holds weights, gradients, optimizer state, and saved activations; inference keeps the weights plus the largest adjacent pair of activation buffers (each layer's buffer dies when the next layer finishes). For the running network at batch 32 that is ~1.3 MB vs ~462 KB, about 3x the memory for identical weights and identical forward arithmetic.

symbols.name: weights
symbols.meaning: persistent parameters; the only term inference keeps

symbols.name: gradients
symbols.meaning: one buffer per parameter; vanishes at inference

symbols.name: optimizer state
symbols.meaning: running statistics per parameter (1 copy momentum, 2 for Adam)

symbols.name: saved activations
symbols.meaning: all layer outputs held for the backward pass; scales with B, depth, width

symbols.name: buffer pair
symbols.meaning: largest adjacent pair of activation buffers; all inference keeps beyond weights

title: Intensity and the roofline bound
caption: FLOPs over bytes moved under a stream-everything traffic model. Batching multiplies the numerator (each weight read serves B examples) while parameter bytes stay fixed, so intensity climbs ~0.5 FLOP/byte at batch 1 toward ~12 at batch 32, both below the ~20 FLOP/byte ridge. The workload is bandwidth-bound: the accelerator's lead is its memory bandwidth, not its multipliers.

symbols.name: arithmetic intensity
symbols.meaning: FLOP per byte moved; what batching raises

symbols.name: FLOPs
symbols.meaning: 2 per MAC per example, times batch

symbols.name: parameter bytes
symbols.meaning: FP32 weights read once per batch; fixed in B, this is the reuse

symbols.name: activation bytes
symbols.meaning: activations written and read; grows with batch

symbols.name: bandwidth slope
symbols.meaning: attainable rate below the ridge point

title: The expected-cost threshold rule
caption: Chow's 1970 reject option: choose the confidence threshold minimizing manual-review fraction times review cost plus misclassified fraction times error cost. Both fractions count all arriving items, so an error rate quoted on accepted items must be scaled by the accepted fraction. When errors are expensive the rule buys review volume; when reviews are expensive it tolerates error.

symbols.name: confidence threshold
symbols.meaning: cutoff on top-class score; below it, items route to review

symbols.name: review fraction
symbols.meaning: share of all arriving items sent to humans

symbols.name: error fraction
symbols.meaning: share of all items misclassified by the automation

symbols.name: per-item costs
symbols.meaning: their ratio, not their absolute values, sets the threshold

title: The chain-rule product
latex: \frac{\partial L}{\partial A^{(l)}} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial A^{(l+1)}}\,\frac{\partial A^{(l+1)}}{\partial A^{(l)}}
caption: Each layer's gradient is a product of local slopes applied in reverse order, so the backward pass consumes saved activations last-to-first. Cascaded over L layers it multiplies L Jacobian factors end to end: factors below 1 vanish exponentially (20 sigmoid layers: 0.25^20 ~ 9e-13), above 1 they explode to Inf then NaN. Numerical range is part of the training contract.

symbols.name: local Jacobian
symbols.meaning: one layer's matrix of slopes; magnitudes near 1 keep the product stable

symbols.name: layer error signal
symbols.meaning: sensitivity of the final loss to this layer's output

symbols.name: factors
symbols.meaning: the depth is also the product length; why initialization scale matters
